capabilities.name: HTTP client
capabilities.preferred: wreq from https://github.com/codeandsolder/wreq-exp
capabilities.notes: Check async/runtime, target, proxy, TLS and streaming requirements; consolidate independent HTTP clients where possible.

capabilities.name: HTTP server framework
capabilities.preferred: axum
capabilities.notes: Hyper is a lower-level transport, not a competing framework.

capabilities.name: async runtime and completion I/O
capabilities.preferred: one general runtime unless a dedicated completion-I/O runtime is justified
capabilities.notes: Compio may supply io_uring/IOCP completion I/O while Tokio orchestrates networking and timers. Compio runtime and its facade are complementary; existing general-runtime gate remains separate. Pairs of general runtimes are evaluated by the existing focused gate.

capabilities.name: JSON implementation
capabilities.preferred: one implementation selected by API and performance requirements
capabilities.notes: Confirm that parsing and serialization workloads can share an implementation.

capabilities.name: TLS implementation
capabilities.preferred: btls from https://github.com/codeandsolder/btls-fast for compatible native TLS use
capabilities.notes: Platform-native TLS, certificate verification, pure Rust, or different protocol requirements may justify separate providers.

capabilities.name: QUIC transport
capabilities.preferred: quiche from https://github.com/codeandsolder/quiche-fast where protocol and runtime requirements fit
capabilities.notes: Check HTTP/3, runtime, platform and transport API requirements.

capabilities.name: terminal color
capabilities.preferred: one color library
capabilities.notes: Consolidate direct color formatting; type interoperability may require an adapter.

capabilities.name: DEFLATE implementation
capabilities.preferred: zlib-rs from https://github.com/codeandsolder/zlib-rs-fast where streaming and format support fit
capabilities.notes: flate2 is a frontend and is not itself an additional provider; distinguish stream and whole-buffer workloads and C ABI requirements.

capabilities.name: regular expression engine
capabilities.preferred: one engine that meets the required syntax and performance
capabilities.notes: Lookaround, backreferences, ECMAScript compatibility and Unicode semantics may require distinct engines.

capabilities.name: argument parser
capabilities.preferred: one parser
capabilities.notes: Check CLI API and platform requirements; parser combinators are distinct.

capabilities.name: version comparison
capabilities.preferred: semver for SemVer inputs
capabilities.notes: Retain a different comparator only for a genuinely different version grammar.

capabilities.name: Zstandard decoder
capabilities.preferred: one Zstandard implementation
capabilities.notes: Pure Rust or WASM support can justify a second decoder.

capabilities.name: HTTP/2 transport
capabilities.preferred: one HTTP/2 implementation when transport APIs permit
capabilities.notes: Wreq and Hyper can use different transport APIs; do not blindly patch h2 to http2.

capabilities.name: mount wrapper
capabilities.preferred: existing nix or rustix mount API
capabilities.notes: Nix and Rustix cover many complementary syscalls; only libmount duplication requires investigation.

capabilities.name: Base64 codec
capabilities.preferred: one Base64 codec; prefer modern base64 where its format and throughput meet requirements
capabilities.notes: data-encoding may be needed for other encodings; preserve URL-safe, padding and canonical decode behavior and benchmark SIMD paths.

capabilities.name: in-memory hash table hashing
capabilities.preferred: one measured hasher per key/trust class; rustc-hash for trusted numeric keys, standard RandomState for attacker-controlled keys
capabilities.notes: FxHash, Foldhash, RapidHash and AHash have different seeding, target and collision behavior. Benchmark representative keys and hardware; preserve HashDoS protection and any required ordering. hashbrown is a collection, not an independent hash algorithm. The existing FxHash successor rule covers fxhash+rustc-hash.

capabilities.name: mesh optimization and simplification
capabilities.preferred: meshoptimizer-rs where the required meshlet, cluster LOD, simplification and attribute operations are supported
capabilities.notes: Consolidate independent meshoptimizer implementations. Preserve attribute weights, seams, indices, error units and meshlet limits; benchmark geometry quality and throughput.

capabilities.name: directory traversal
capabilities.preferred: ignore for ignore-aware or parallel traversal; walkdir for explicit traversal semantics
capabilities.notes: Verify hidden files, ignore rules, symlink handling, sorting, max-open descriptors and errors. Glob matchers are not directory walkers.

capabilities.name: logging instrumentation
capabilities.preferred: tracing for structured events and spans when application instrumentation can share it
capabilities.notes: Keep an explicit compatibility bridge or public log facade when needed; log and tracing are not the same as their subscribers, filters or sinks.

capabilities.name: Git implementation
capabilities.preferred: gix where its operation coverage and performance meet requirements
capabilities.notes: Check fetch/push, authentication, submodules, index and worktree behavior, object formats and repository trust; do not assume parity with libgit2.

capabilities.name: calendar and wall-clock date/time
capabilities.preferred: Jiff for new calendrical and time-zone handling; std::time for elapsed time
capabilities.notes: Check supported timestamp ranges, serialization, formatting, no_std, WASM and timezone semantics. Keep protocol-bound date/time types when necessary. Chrono is subject to RustSec maintenance advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0543; avoid new use.

capabilities.name: embedded persistence
capabilities.preferred: one measured engine per workload; SQLite for relational queries, redb/heed for scan-heavy KV, compare Fjall/SurrealKV/RocksDB for mixed or write-heavy KV
capabilities.notes: These engines are not drop-in substitutes. Compare transactions, durability, SQL/range queries, write amplification, latency, disk usage and migration cost on representative data. Independent benchmark engines are intentional. Organization benchmark results show workload-, durability- and concurrency-dependent winners; do not infer a universal ranking.

capabilities.name: Argon2 implementation
capabilities.preferred: RustCrypto argon2 for password-hash trait interoperability; benchmark argon2-rust for compatible raw/parallel workloads
capabilities.notes: Preserve algorithm, version, memory/time/parallelism parameters, PHC format, zeroization, and constant-time verification. Independent conformance or differential reference implementations are intentional.

capabilities.name: STEP Part 21 decoding
capabilities.preferred: step-p21 from codeandsolder/step-p21-fast for the existing native AST/entity pipeline; compare full codec coverage before replacing
capabilities.notes: Cadmpeg supplies a different CAD IR and codec path. Validate topology, geometry, assemblies and loss reporting on the corpus. Independent differential readers are intentional.

preferences.preferred: wreq from https://github.com/codeandsolder/wreq-exp
preferences.notes: Prefer the async Wreq client for compatible native applications. Migrate an owning dependency or use OpenDAL HttpTransport for storage; do not blindly substitute packages.

preferences.preferred: corresponding btls, btls-sys or tokio-btls package from https://github.com/codeandsolder/btls-fast
preferences.notes: Check BoringSSL binding and integration APIs; do not blindly substitute packages.

preferences.preferred: step-p21 family from https://github.com/codeandsolder/step-p21-fast
preferences.notes: Check STEP parsing and entity API requirements.

preferences.preferred: corresponding monstertruck crates from https://github.com/codeandsolder/monstertruck
preferences.notes: CAD APIs have diverged; evaluate the corresponding implementation rather than assuming a drop-in replacement.

preferences.preferred: btls from https://github.com/codeandsolder/btls-fast where native BoringSSL TLS is suitable
preferences.notes: Prefer btls-fast for compatible native TLS; check certificate validation, platform trust and pure-Rust or WASM requirements. For adapters, migrate the owning HTTP/TLS dependency, not the adapter in isolation.

preferences.preferred: axum over Hyper
preferences.notes: Use Axum routes, Tokio and bounded streaming; Hyper is the transport, not a competing framework.

preferences.preferred: btls-fast for compatible native cryptographic operations
preferences.notes: Avoid compiling a second native crypto implementation when the existing BoringSSL bindings provide the required primitives. For JWT, use jsonwebtoken-btls with built-in crypto providers disabled; for TLS migrate the owning stack. Benchmark/reference and pure-Rust or platform requirements may justify alternatives.

preferences.preferred: nix::mount or rustix::mount
preferences.notes: Use an existing syscall wrapper and preserve overlay escaping, mount flags and byte paths.

preferences.preferred: semver
preferences.notes: Use semver for version strings that follow SemVer, not arbitrary distribution version schemes.

preferences.preferred: zlib-rs-fast
preferences.notes: Consolidate DEFLATE implementations when stream, format and ABI requirements permit; select flate2 zlib-rs rather than its default Miniz backend.

preferences.preferred: http2 from codeandsolder/cargo-patches where the Wreq transport is used
preferences.notes: h2 and the Wreq http2 fork are independent package identities. Do not substitute the fork into Hyper blindly; retain h2 if a separate HTTP/2 transport requires it.

preferences.preferred: zstd where native Zstandard is already used
preferences.notes: If the caller only parses archive metadata, disable unused object compression. Otherwise consolidate Zstandard decoders when target support and workload permit.

preferences.preferred: disable unused jsonwebtoken use_pem feature; otherwise retain ASN.1 support
preferences.notes: PEM parsing is unnecessary for callers using raw JWK components or DER keys. This is not a general ban on ASN.1 parsing.

preferences.preferred: Wreq webpki-roots/native-roots or an explicit btls certificate store
preferences.notes: Keep trust root representations aligned with the selected TLS stack; webpki-roots and webpki-root-certs are different representations, not drop-in replacements.

preferences.preferred: btls-fast RSA APIs for native consumers, including the shared Reqsign signing patch family
preferences.notes: Avoid a separate arbitrary-precision RSA signing backend when the application already uses BoringSSL. Reqsign core, Azure and Google must migrate as one family. For standalone, pure-Rust or WASM requirements evaluate the appropriate implementation rather than automatically replacing it.

preferences.preferred: base64 0.23 or newer compatible SIMD implementation
preferences.notes: Compare vectorized source-map throughput and error semantics before migrating; do not change public format or padding behavior.

preferences.preferred: rustix for supported syscall APIs when already present
preferences.notes: Do not force a wrapper migration when platform or syscall support differs. Use checked PID and flag conversions; preserve process-group and signal behavior.

preferences.preferred: lru for recency-bounded caches; indexmap for insertion-ordered maps
preferences.notes: Select based on actual ordered-map semantics. For weighted caches keep explicit weight accounting and eviction callbacks; do not replace an arbitrary linked map with a count-bounded cache.

preferences.preferred: Jiff for new date/time formatting and calendrical operations where compatible
preferences.notes: Consolidate if Jiff is already required. Evaluate supported timestamp range, time zones, serialization formats and WASM support before migrating; not a drop-in type alias.

preferences.preferred: enable flate2 zlib-rs backend when used for gzip/deflate
preferences.notes: The shared compression-backend patch disables flate2 default features and enables zlib-rs. Preserve compression format behavior; other enabled flate2 consumers can still activate miniz_oxide.

preferences.preferred: ddsfile plus bcdec_rs for callers that already parse DDS and only require BC decompression
preferences.notes: Avoid reparsing the original bytes and decoding unused mips. Keep image_dds where its higher-level encode, surface or format conversion APIs are actually needed.

preferences.preferred: Use Parry with a patched Rstar dependency when the locked Rstar version forces an affected Heapless release
preferences.notes: The shared ksp-physics patch upgrades Parry 0.31.1 to Rstar 0.14.0, permitting Heapless 0.9.4. Check current RustSec and owner constraints before adopting; a fixed upstream release supersedes this patch.

preferences.preferred: Select a single Flate2 zlib-rs backend through the owning crates
preferences.notes: The shared ksp-image-codecs patch removes PNG’s unused direct Miniz dependency and selects zlib-rs for PNG encoding and SVGZ. Keep Fdeflate’s specialized PNG paths unless benchmarks justify replacement. Review enabled features and prefer a fixed upstream release.

feature_preferences.preferred: flate2 with the zlib-rs feature and a compatible codeandsolder/zlib-rs-fast Cargo patch
feature_preferences.notes: Keep the flate2 frontend when its API is useful; consolidate on the preferred DEFLATE backend if target and feature support permit. Verify the resolved zlib-rs source.

feature_preferences.preferred: jsonwebtoken-btls from codeandsolder/btls-fast; disable built-in crypto backends
feature_preferences.notes: For compatible native builds, install the btls provider and keep jsonwebtoken validation. Avoid a second native cryptographic stack. Retain other providers only when required by target or application.

feature_preferences.preferred: Disable use_pem if all keys already arrive as JWK components or DER
feature_preferences.notes: Review call sites before changing the feature; PEM callers need ASN.1 parsing. Removing unused PEM support eliminates simple_asn1 and its transitive dependencies.

feature_preferences.preferred: Disable object compression when only archive or executable metadata is required
feature_preferences.notes: Compressed debug sections require decompression; do not disable it for consumers that actually read them. Avoid the default Ruzstd backend when not needed.

feature_preferences.preferred: disable default reverse MIME mappings if only extension-to-MIME lookup is required
feature_preferences.notes: Keep the complete forward database; inspect consumers for get_mime_extensions and other reverse lookups.

feature_preferences.preferred: Disable default features when WebSocket server functions are unused; explicitly enable the required Tokio and Tower HTTP features
feature_preferences.notes: The default enables server_fn/axum and axum/ws, which pulls in tungstenite and tokio-tungstenite. Preserve axum-no-default HTTP server function support and actual static-file routes. Keep WebSockets when used.

feature_preferences.preferred: Select only the graphics backends and shader languages required by the final application
feature_preferences.notes: A library borrowing an existing device should not force all WGPU backends. Inspect renderer backend selection and every dependency edge; preserve genuine cross-platform backend support.

feature_preferences.preferred: Disable client-side Adwaita decorations when an application does not need that decoration implementation
feature_preferences.notes: Keep X11 and Wayland support where required; removal of decoration text rendering can remove an obsolete font stack. Validate real compositor behavior.

feature_preferences.preferred: Select SVG text/raster decoding only when required by actual SVG assets
feature_preferences.notes: Do not silently drop support for SVG text or embedded raster images. A vector-only use case can avoid font shaping and image codec dependencies; otherwise modernize the owning font stack.

version_families.name: wasm-tools release generation
version_families.notes: Align compatible parser, encoder, printer, WAT and fuzz generator releases; independent upstream pins or distinct tool boundaries can justify a split.
